--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_relaxed_caveman_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Add a relaxed caveman graph: cliques whose edges are randomly rewired. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_relaxed_caveman_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Add a relaxed caveman graph: cliques whose edges are randomly rewired. title: >- [Graph.add_relaxed_caveman_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a relaxed caveman graph: cliques whose edges are randomly rewired. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a relaxed caveman graph: cliques whose edges are randomly rewired. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16635-L16799){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_relaxed_caveman_graph( num_cliques, clique_size, p, seed=None, community_attr="community", type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Relaxed caveman graph](../assets/graphs/add-relaxed-caveman-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three relaxed caveman graphs built from three complete graphs on four nodes, each in its own color, at rewiring probability p=0, 0.2, and 0.5. At p=0 the cliques are separate; as p grows, more edges are rewired to random nodes and show up as plain edges between the cliques (3 at p=0.2 and 6 at p=0.5), while the total stays 18." width="100%"} Starts from `num_cliques` separate cliques of `clique_size` nodes (the caveman graph, see `add_caveman_graph()`) and visits every edge once, cliques in order. With probability `p` the edge `(u, v)` is rewired to `(u, x)`, where `x` is a node chosen uniformly at random from the whole graph; the rewiring is skipped if `x` is `u` itself or already a neighbor of `u`. The edge count never changes, but as `p` grows more edges leave their cave: `p=0` keeps the caveman graph and `p=1` approaches a random graph. The process follows NetworkX's `relaxed_caveman_graph()`. Each node's original cave (`0`, `1`, ...) is stored in the `community_attr=` node attribute, so that the planted communities can be compared with what a detection method finds as the rewiring blurs them. The caves are created in order, each as a consecutive run of node IDs. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Relaxed caveman graphs are useful for: - benchmarking community detection as structure fades, by sweeping `p=` and comparing the result with the planted caves - modeling tightly knit groups with occasional ties to outsiders - small-world experiments in which a few random edges shorten the paths between groups ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [num_cliques]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of cliques. Must be at least `1`. [clique_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in each clique. Must be at least `1`. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of rewiring each edge, between `0` and `1`. Roughly a fraction `p` of the edges end up leaving their cave. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [community_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's cave. Default is `"community"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `num_cliques=` or `clique_size=` is less than `1`, or `p=` is not between `0` and `1`. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~add_caveman_graph`) : Add the caves without rewiring. [](`~add_connected_caveman_graph`) : Join the caves in a ring by rewiring one edge in each. [](`~partition_quality`) : Measure how many edges stay inside the planted caves. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The graph starts as separate caves, complete graphs, and each edge is then moved, with probability `p`, to a random node elsewhere. Rewiring keeps the edge count of five caves of six nodes at `5 * 15 = 75`: ::: {#dfe0e0c8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_relaxed_caveman_graph( num_cliques=5, clique_size=6, p=0.2, seed=7 ) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (30, 75) ``` ::: ::: The share of edges that stay inside their cave (the coverage of the planted partition) falls as `p=` grows: ::: {#1dccd0a4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} coverage = [] for p in (0.0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.6): g = ec.Graph().add_relaxed_caveman_graph( num_cliques=5, clique_size=6, p=p, seed=7 ) coverage.append(round(g.partition_quality("community")[0], 2)) coverage ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [1.0, 0.92, 0.75, 0.53] ``` ::: ::: ### A little rewiring or a lot With `p=0.1` on the left the caves are still clear, with a few edges between them. With `p=0.6` on the right most edges have left their cave, and the colors, one per cave, are mixed through the drawing: ::: {#658cec2c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} light = ec.Graph().add_relaxed_caveman_graph( num_cliques=5, clique_size=6, p=0.1, seed=7 ) heavy = ec.Graph().add_relaxed_caveman_graph( num_cliques=5, clique_size=6, p=0.6, seed=7 ) [round(g.modularity("community"), 2) for g in (light, heavy)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [0.72, 0.33] ``` ::: ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#db3a8d22 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} light.plot( color_by="community", show_labels=False, width=320, height=320, legend=False, seed=1, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
